slides.label: Introduction
slides.narration: Let us calculate the density of a ceramic sample and keep every unit consistent.

slides.label: Equation
slides.narration: Density equals mass divided by volume.

params.caption: Use kilograms and cubic metres for kilograms per cubic metre.

slides.label: Worked solution
slides.narration: Substitute zero point three six zero kilograms and one point five times ten to the minus four cubic metres.

slides.label: Retrieval summary
slides.narration: The sample density is two thousand four hundred kilograms per cubic metre.

params.heading: Pause and recall
points: Give the unit with the answer
